title: Resume the same reading session after reopening the app
description:
## What?

Keep the reading place and study work when the app is closed.

## Why?

A learner should be free to stop and return without losing work.

## Done when

- Reopening on the same browser restores the paragraph or thread.
- Highlights, notes, drafts, replies, and nested threads remain intact.
- Read marks and visual controls keep their state.
- If saving fails, the learner sees a clear error and can keep a copy.

title: Keep every question linked to its exact highlight
description:
## What?

Link each question to the text that led to it, in the book or a reply.

## Why?

The learner needs to trace an idea back to its source when they review it.

## Done when

- Any selected text can start a thread with a visible source highlight.
- The highlight opens its thread, and the thread returns to the same text.
- Deeper threads keep their parent links, replies, notes, and visuals.
- Revised notes and questions keep earlier work for review.

title: Resume private study on a computer or iPad
description:
## What?

Host the app on Cloudflare and keep study work in sync across devices.

## Why?

The learner may read on an iPad and return to a computer later.

## Done when

- Only the signed-in owner can access books and study work.
- A session closed on one device resumes on the other.
- Offline edits and edits from two devices do not silently erase work.
- The saved study work can be exported and restored.

title: Ask the assistant and get replies inside the thread
description:
## What?

Ask Codex about the current passage and read its reply in the app.

## Why?

Copying questions to another app breaks the flow of study.

## Done when

- Replies use the passage, selected text, and relevant thread history.
- Follow-ups stay in the thread unless the learner starts a new branch.
- Replies and source links remain saved after the app closes.
- Failed replies can be retried without losing or repeating the question.
- No follow-up questions are added without being asked for.

title: See the tokens and cost of each assistant reply
description:
## What?

Show what each reply costs and the total spent on study.

## Why?

The learner needs to know what they are spending as they use the assistant.

## Done when

- Each call records input, cached input, and output tokens where reported.
- Costs include image and tool charges when those are used.
- A small usage view shows each reply and the running total.
- Unknown charges are shown as unknown, never as free.
- Retries count the work billed without counting a call twice.

title: Read a full checked chapter one paragraph at a time
description:
## What?

Turn a Modern Robotics chapter into clear web text, equations, and figures.

## Why?

A full chapter will show whether the reading flow works beyond the sample.

## Done when

- Paragraphs, equations, figures, and source pages match the book.
- The learner chooses when to move on and can return to any read passage.
- Chapter order and reading history stay saved without a mastery gate.
- The layout uses web text and visuals rather than full PDF pages.

title: Ask for a visual explanation within a thread
description:
## What?

Let the learner ask for a diagram, image, or a visual they can move.

## Why?

Some ideas are easier to grasp through motion or a picture than text alone.

## Done when

- Visualize adds a useful answer to the same thread.
- Visuals and their controls stay linked to the source answer.
- New images are saved and their costs are included.
- Video links use a checked start time for the relevant part.

title: Read, highlight, and follow threads comfortably on iPad
description:
## What?

Make the reading flow work well with touch, in both iPad orientations.

## Why?

Reading and selecting text should feel natural away from a desk.

## Done when

- Text selection, highlights, notes, and thread links work with touch.
- The keyboard leaves the question and reply controls within reach.
- Equations and visuals fit the screen or have clear local scrolling.
- The same spare interface works on a computer and an iPad.

title: Turn book exercises into saved assignments with hints
description:
## What?

Give the learner book exercises at the right point, with hints on request.

## Why?

Trying a problem helps the learner test ideas and find gaps.

## Done when

- Assignments link to the book exercise and the relevant reading.
- Attempts and notes stay saved for later review.
- Hints build in steps and do not show the full solution by default.
- The learner can revisit a problem without losing earlier attempts.

title: Add another book without changing the learning flow
description:
## What?

Add a second book with its own chapters, threads, notes, and progress.

## Why?

This app is for learning across books, not only Modern Robotics.

## Done when

- A second book can be added and its reading order checked.
- Each book keeps its own source links, history, and study work.
- Switching books returns to the saved place in each one.
- An updated source does not silently move an old highlight.

title: Check the original PDF page while reading
description:
## What?

Open the exact book page from the PDF while reading a paragraph.

## Why?

The learner may want to check the source text or see the whole page.

## Done when

- The source page stays hidden until the learner opens it.
- The page matches the current paragraph, with the book's layout intact.
- Closing the source leaves the reading place, question, and notes as they were.
